jobs.title: Director of Grants and Compliance
jobs.description:
Are you dedicated to empowering and supporting youth, regardless of their background? We're searching for passionate individuals to make a positive impact on the lives of foster youth. Become an integral part of their transformative journey and join the First Place for Youth team.

About First Place for Youth, We’re a leading non-profit organization dedicated to supporting foster youth in their transition to adulthood, with a focus on education, employment, and housing. We believe that all young people deserve the opportunity to thrive and lead successful, independent lives. Our comprehensive programs empower foster youth to overcome the unique challenges they face and build the skills, confidence, and connections they need to succeed.

Why Work at First Place For Youth:

Meaningful Impact
: Help to transform the lives of foster youth on the cusp of adulthood. Your role will support them in their journey to conquer challenges, achieve independence, and fulfill their aspirations.
Innovative Approach:
We thrive on innovation, pushing the boundaries of foster care support. Your voice here matters, and you’ll contribute to programs that redefine the futures of these young lives.
Collaborative and Supportive Environment:
Embrace a dynamic and supportive workplace, where every team member is valued. Together, we're a force dedicated to uplifting youth. Expect professional growth, fueled by teamwork and collaboration.
Comprehensive Benefits:
We value the well-being of our employees and offer a comprehensive benefits package. From health and wellness benefits to retirement plans, we ensure that our team members are taken care of so they can focus on their important work supporting foster youth.
Culture of Diversity and Inclusion:
We celebrate diversity in every form. At First Place for Youth, inclusivity reigns, creating a workplace where all voices are heard, respected, and empowered.

Position Summary:
The position of Director of Contracts and Compliance is a vital role of a growing public contracts team at First Place. Working closely with the VP of Contracts and Compliance, this dynamic role supports and guides many aspects of public contracting—including working with multiple local, county, and statewide funders, providing critical lead guidance and support on procurement processes, and overseeing contract management and compliance across California with a focus on Los Angeles. The Director will work with the VP of Contracts and Compliance to shape, plan, and implement First Place’s public contracts strategy, which includes ensuring the solicitation of new and existing procurements, compliance processes, and building and maintaining funder partnerships for approximately 25-30 contracts totaling $30 Million Dollars annually. The Director will oversee two members of the Contracts team: the Contract and Compliance Manager and the Contracts Associate. Currently, the Contracts and Compliance Department is responsible for identifying new funding sources, submitting proposals for published RFP’s, maintaining existing contracts, ensuring program regulatory compliance, and representing the agency in various public facing convenings. The department explores various public funding opportunities including the use of CalAIM as an additional revenue source. The Director is a new position to build capacity for the department to expand its presence and oversight of all public contracts, particularly in the Los Angeles region as the agency sets out to expand programming in multiple jurisdictions in the coming years. The Director will be the agency lead for the Los Angeles contracts as well as resource and technical expert for Community Care Licensing compliance.

Duties + Responsibilities:

Public Funding Procurement

As directed by the VP, oversee the procurement process for public funds from inception to submission including researching, writing, and packaging proposals with support from the Contracts Team.
Stay informed on latest trends within relevant funding industries such as child welfare, homelessness, affordable housing, CalAIM, juvenile justice, and workforce development.
The Director is expected to be able to write and oversee the assembly and final submission.
The Director may delegate some procurements to the Manager as lead such as workforce related opportunities.

Contract Management and Funder Relations

The Director plans, develops and directs staff in the preparation of budget line item narratives, recommendations and justifications based on various agency analyses for annual, supplemental and multi-year requests.
Work effectively with agency leaders to develop and manage calendars and tracking mechanisms to ensure that all contract development, implementation and reporting is accurate and timely.
Develop effective collaboration between fiscal and program to develop contract components in timely manner.
Ensure congruency between program and fiscal components of contracts; providing final check for accuracy before contracts leave the agency.
Track contract signatures, publish contract status grid/calendar and communicate proactively with stakeholders, file and maintain official contract library.
Provide administrative documents in support of contracts (e.g. corporate compliance plan, cultural competence plan, insurance documents, etc.) as needed.
Provide each manager with a list of important dates for contract compliance (e.g. various reports required and dates due) at start of each contract year.
Build and/or maintain relationship with funders; particularly in Los Angeles and attend relevant meetings and convenings in person.

Contract Compliance

Provide final oversight of compliance activities performed by the Contracts Team, particularly in the area of agency single audit for client eligibility checks and new monitoring of Los Angeles contracts.
Maintain or create efficient processes for improvements
Ensure and lead team on various new compliance processes across various jurisdictions.
Leadership support for all on site monitoring and reviews by funders.

Team Management and Supervision

Provide overall leadership to the Contracts team, with one direct report. Motivate, inspire, manage and develop staff so they continue to be informed and passionate about our mission, and committed to First Place’s core competencies.
Utilize a strengths-based approach to management, provide ongoing guidance and coaching to members of the team.

Other Duties and Projects as assigned

Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree required in human services, social work, social sciences, public administration, public policy, or relevant area. Master’s degree preferred.
8+ years of progressive leadership experience in grant and contracts procurement and compliance within public sector with 5+ years of direct supervisory experience managing multi-level teams.
Minimum of 8 years of experience in nonprofit or government agency including strong familiarity with best practices in engagement and stewardship of government funders.
Understanding and experience with government competitive bid processes.
Minimum of 5 years managing public contracts within the fields of child welfare, homelessness, affordable housing, social services, and/or juvenile justice.
Must be a strong grant writer with experience writing government grants.
Prior program budget management experience is required for this role.
Understanding of the child welfare and homeless systems preferred.
Understanding or experience in direct services to relevant vulnerable populations such as transition age youth, homeless, families required.
A track record of success managing staff and collaborating with peers.
Ability to think strategically, then communicate and implement innovative ideas successfully.
Ability to interpret social science data.
Ability to interpret complex regulations and explain.
Highly organized with superior attention to detail and project management skills.
Ability to multitask in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
Ability to take initiative, be proactive, and independent.
Excellent communication skills, including written, interpersonal, and presentation skills for potential funders.
Commitment to the mission of First Place for Youth.
Computer/Software skills.
Availability for occasional evening and weekend work and some travel as needed.

Foster strong relationships with physicians, community leaders, board members, and key stakeholders.
Create alignment between people, processes, and strategies to achieve organizational objectives.
Recruit, develop, mentor, and retain high-performing leadership teams.
Promote a culture of accountability, engagement, and continuous improvement.
Communicate organizational priorities, performance metrics, and strategic initiatives effectively throughout the organization.

FOX Entertainment With a legacy spanning nearly 40 years, FOX Entertainment is one of the world’s most recognizable media brands and a leading global creator of multi-genre content across broadcast, streaming, digital and emerging platforms. Through these strategic initiatives, the company is investing earlier in emerging ideas and new forms of audience engagement, while maintaining the ability to grow successful concepts into premium franchises across broadcast, streaming and global platforms. A prolific content creator and production partner, FOX Entertainment collaborates with leading studios, creators, and platforms worldwide to produce and distribute premium content at scale across broadcast, streaming, and digital ecosystems, while continuing to grow its portfolio of owned IP and next-generation storytelling formats.

JOB DESCRIPTION

Fox Entertainment is seeking an Executive Director, Business & Legal Affairs to lead and support a broad range of strategic dealmaking and legal matters across creator partnerships, production, and emerging technology initiatives. This role will serve as a senior legal and business advisor, partnering closely with business and legal affairs leadership and key stakeholders to structure, negotiate, and execute complex agreements in a rapidly evolving media landscape.

The department sits at the intersection of traditional entertainment, the creator economy, and technology-driven production. The ideal candidate is a highly versatile, business-minded executive who thrives in an entrepreneurial environment within a large media company. This individual combines strong strategic judgment with the ability to independently manage a high volume of complex, day-to-day matters; build trusted relationships with internal and external stakeholders; and develop practical solutions that advance business objectives while appropriately managing risk.

Support the negotiation, drafting, and execution of a broad range of complex agreements, including creator, production, talent, licensing, content, and technology-related deals

Partner cross-functionally with production, ad sales, technology, finance, business development, and other teams to structure and execute partnerships and strategic initiatives

Contribute to the development of technology-related policy, guidelines, and governance frameworks as the business models in this space take shape
Navigate a high degree of ambiguity, applying sound judgment to novel legal and business questions where clear precedent doesn't yet exist
Build and maintain strong relationships with creators, producers, agents, attorneys, technology partners, and other external stakeholders
Manage multiple high-priority projects simultaneously while exercising sound judgment in a fast-paced and evolving environment

JD degree and active membership in the California Bar; candidates eligible for Registered In-House Counsel status under Rule 9.46 will also be considered.
10+ years of progressively responsible legal experience, including substantial in-house entertainment, media, technology, or related transactional experience; top-tier law firm experience
Significant experience independently negotiating and drafting complex production, talent, creator, licensing, content, and/or technology agreements
Demonstrated ability to advise senior business leaders and influence strategic decisions through practical, commercially minded legal counsel
Strong understanding of entertainment rights, production, talent, and evolving digital media business models
Excellent legal judgment, negotiation, drafting, communication, and interpersonal skills

Ability to lead complex matters from strategy through execution, manage competing priorities, and remain composed under pressure

NICE TO HAVE BUT NOT A DEALBREAKER

Experience supporting creator economy, digital media, platform, or technology-enabled production initiatives

Company Description

The Downtown Albany Business Improvement District (BID) is a 501(c)3 nonprofit corporation. Since 1996, it has served as the principal advocate for property owners, businesses, service providers, employees, and residents on 50 blocks in the heart of downtown Albany.

With a 20-person Board, a staff of 3, and an annual budget of approximately $800,000, the BID delivers programs in marketing, special events, clean & safe initiatives, visual improvements, and economic development. The organization’s mission is to restore, promote, and maintain the character and viability of downtown Albany and improve the quality of life and overall image for those who live in, work in and visit the Capital City.

The Opportunity

The new Executive Director will lead the organization and Downtown into its next chapter. Working closely with an engaged Board and a dynamic team of professionals, the ED will provide strategic leadership to guide the continued transformation of downtown Albany into a premier urban destination. This is an extraordinary opportunity for a visionary and entrepreneurial leader to successfully drive the BID’s mission by providing expertise on downtown issues, capitalizing on opportunities, and working with the BID Board of Directors, stakeholders, and the City in creating and implementing strategic planning initiatives to develop and sustain a vibrant downtown in which to live, work, play, and invest for all.

The Ideal Candidate

The ideal ED for this role is a strategic, mission-driven, dynamic, inspiring, and collaborative leader, possessing a balance of strategic vision and practical management ability. Qualified candidates will have proficiency in implementing strategic economic development initiatives, a proven track record in special events creation and management and strategic communications and marketing, strong administration and fiscal management, and positive communications and relationship building/management skills.

Experience

· Senior-level leadership experience in downtown management, economic development, nonprofit or related sectors, and teams/staff.
· Experience navigating public-private partnerships with city agencies and elected officials.
· Knowledge of the unique challenges of downtown Albany or urban areas.
· Strong financial acumen and experience overseeing budgets.
· Demonstrated success managing large-scale projects within complex organizational structures.
· Exceptional communication, interpersonal, and stakeholder engagement skills. Proven ability to build trust and consensus among diverse and sometimes competing stakeholders.
· Solid fundraising and grant writing experience.
· Comfort working in a highly visible, public-facing role with media, elected officials, and business leaders, including in moments of disagreement or scrutiny.

Responsibilities

· Lead a respected nonprofit with a strong reputation. Work with our engaged Board and experienced staff to develop work plans that translate the organization's mission and vision into realistic goals and objectives, ensuring successful achievement of goals and objectives established by the Board.
· Lead, mentor, and manage staff by fostering a collaborative, high-performing workplace. Provide clear direction, professional development opportunities, performance management, and team leadership to support organizational success.
· Provide oversight and management for day-to-day operations of the organization's programs, including administrative/human resource management, fiscal, operations, public safety, economic development, and capital improvements.
· Develop an annual budget (in conjunction with the Budget & Finance Committee and staff) that is attainable and consistent with the goals and objectives established by the Board and operate within that budget. Ensure compliance with legal and regulatory requirements.
· Serving as an ambassador for the organization and Downtown with the media, elected officials, BID stakeholders, and the City of Albany, as well as be an advocate for downtown issues. Maintain clear internal and external communication and information flow.
· Cultivate and maintain effective relationships with property owners, businesses, public officials, community and business leaders, and the media.
· Prioritize, plan, drive, and monitor projects to ensure appropriateness to mission and vision, and effective completion by deadlines established by the Board.
· Expand revenue sources through fundraising, sponsorships, merchandise, and grant writing.
Education and Preferred Experience
· Education consistent with demonstrated, quantifiable leadership in marketing, business development, events, fundraising, strategic planning, fiscal management, real estate and economic development.

This is a full-time, exempt salaried position with occasional nights and weekends as needed. It is a fully in person/in office position. Competitive benefits. Salary is $105,000 per year.

How to Apply

Letter of application addressing the candidate’s qualifications, resume, and contact information for personal references should be forwarded to: Georgette Steffens, Downtown Albany Business Improvement District, 21 Lodge Street, Albany, NY 12207, or via email at gsteffens@downtownalbany.org.

Summary

New Settlement is a community-led, mission-driven settlement house. For more than 30 years, we have partnered with youth and families in the Southwest Bronx to expand access to opportunities and resources that support individual and community well-being. Our work includes award-winning programs in after-school education, workforce development, college readiness, health and fitness, and member-driven community organizing for better housing and safer schools.

About The Organization

Rooted in the Bronx, we stand with community members to break systemic barriers, advance justice, promote leadership and strengthen neighborhoods. By ensuring agency around education, employment, housing, wellness and creative expression, we help cultivate an equitable society where individuals and families have the power to use their voice to create the change they wish to see.

New Settlement partners with residents to expand access to opportunity, address barriers and inequities, and support the goals and priorities that young people and families have for themselves and their community. Created in 1989, New Settlement has since evolved into a robust social service organization offering a range of community-based services in education, college access, youth development, arts, workforce development, community organizing, and wellness. New Settlement works to support the community's inherent strengths, aspirations, and assets through close collaboration with a wide range of neighborhood, borough, and city-wide educational institutions, housing and community development organizations, businesses, youth development and social service agencies.

What You'll Do

We are looking for a dynamic, strategic, and hands-on Executive Director committed to driving impact for and in partnership with our community. The ED will serve as the organization's chief executive. They will implement an overarching community justice vision, drive organizational excellence, and oversee strategic priorities, fundraising, and partnerships. Additionally, the ED will be a champion for the New Settlement team and cultivate a collaborative and inclusive culture.

This position is based in the Bronx, overseeing staff across several community based locations.

Qualifications

At least 10 years of serving in a senior leadership role (e.g. Executive Director level) at a non-profit direct service or social justice organization.
A genuine belief in the strengths and potential of the Southwest Bronx, and an eagerness to partner with community stakeholders to realize that potential
An authentic passion and commitment for New Settlement's mission to strengthen neighborhoods through youth and family development, community organizing, workforce training, education, and community service
Outstanding organizational leadership skills, with an ability to articulate a clear and inspiring vision while managing, coaching, and developing a high-performing team and engaged board of directors
Strong management experience with a demonstrated track record of implementing systems and processes that elevate performance and increase the team's connection to the organization and its mission
Achieves strategic clarity and maintains operational velocity during periods of change or incomplete information, pivots thoughtfully as new intelligence becomes available.
Maintains energy, enthusiasm, and optimism about their work during bright moments and through challenges
Collaborative and empathetic approach to team leadership, and a demonstrated capacity to partner well with others and influence leaders
Experience overseeing the financial management and financial strategy of an organization (i.e. developing budgets, creating financial reports, reporting financial health to the board)
Strong appetite to lead fundraising efforts, ideally with a demonstrated track record of success leading fundraising in a nonprofit setting
Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to strengthen teams and serve as a strong external representative for the organization

Duties

Strategic Leadership & Vision

Drive the organization's vision of building equitable futures in the Bronx through programs in education, employment, wellness, and organizing.
Foster a culture of support, accountability and impact, enabling and inspiring staff to track and meet goals
Oversee the development and retention of staff, ensuring that the team has the robust skills and capabilities necessary to deliver outcomes for our community
Oversee strategic planning, brand elevation, and program expansion to adapt to evolving neighborhood needs.
Work closely with the Board Chair, Settlement Housing Fund's President, and New Settlement's Board of Directors on governance, fiduciary oversight, and organizational policies.

Programmatic & Operational Oversight

Lead assessment, optimization, and implementation of organizational systems to ensure that programmatic and operational models reflect high standards for impact and a community service orientation
Work with program leads to define, operationalize, and measure programmatic excellence in the areas of:
Youth & Family Development: After school programs, summer programs, Young Men Establishing the Narrative (YMEN), Program for Girls and Young Women (PGYW)
Community Organizing: Community Action for Safe Apartments (CASA), Parent Action Committee (PAC)
Workforce Development: YouthBuild construction training, Young Adult Opportunity Initiative (YAOI) job readiness training and mentorship
College & Career Access: Community Schools, College Access Center, Student Success Center
Community Services: The New Settlement Community Center, food pantry initiatives, and early childhood education partnerships.

Identify and pursue strategic partnerships to enhance the impact and reach of key programs
Work with outsourced finance lead and in-house contract manager to direct the annual budget, ensure compliance with government/funder mandates, and oversee facilities, HR, and administrative operations.

Fundraising & External Relations

Lead growth and diversification of revenue streams, including government performance contracts, foundation grants, private philanthropy, and corporate partnerships.
Represent New Settlement locally and citywide, maintaining strong coalitions and relationships with diverse stakeholders, including local organizers, community leaders, and elected officials.
Maintain close operational and strategic alignment with partners, including Settlement Housing Fund and local coalitions

Who You'll Work With

ABOUT BREAKTHROUGH NEW YORK

Breakthrough New York empowers motivated students from low-income communities to achieve a college degree and reach their fullest potential. Our tuition-free program supports over 500 students and their families from 7th grade through college. We accept middle school students who are furthest from high-quality educational opportunities yet show promise and potential: 99% of students identify as persons of color and 56% will be the first in their families to graduate college.

As a ten-year program, Breakthrough New York supports students and their families through key transition points in their academic journeys. We provide academic enrichment through summer and after-school opportunities; coach students to gain admissions into selective high schools and colleges, and expose students to diverse interests and careers so they can shape their own trajectories.

In addition to nurturing individual talent, we cultivate a thriving community of like-minded peers and mentors who encourage each other’s ambitions and passions. Personalized mentorship and holistic support are signature elements of our model, with over 200 near-peer seasonal staff and volunteers who work with students at each stage of our continuum.

The Breakthrough model works: 94% of Breakthrough students enroll in college preparatory high schools, and 97% are on track to graduate from college in four-six years. Learn more at Breakthrough New York's website .

ABOUT THE POSITION

Reporting directly to the Chief Development Officer (CDO), the Director of Grants and Communications Manager will join the development team to collaboratively raise an organizational budget of $4.024M annually, and oversee a portfolio of $1.2M - $1.5M current and prospective opportunities. This position is responsible for renewing and identifying new grants from institutional partners. As a skilled written communicator and project manager, they will work closely with the CDO and Executive Director to meet ambitious giving goals by managing and growing existing public, foundation, and corporate foundation funding, identifying and pursuing new funding opportunities, and supporting organization communications. This role is crucial for ensuring the organization's financial sustainability and ability to carry out Breakthrough New York’s mission effectively.

Craft compelling and thorough grant proposals and reports that effectively communicate the organization's mission, programs, and impact to current and potential institutional donors.
Create standardized templates for grant proposals and reports to ensure consistency and efficiency for all development team usage.
Curate and update a repository of approved language for proposals and program-related pitch materials.
Facilitate data requests to the Chief Program Officer, operations requests to the Senior Director of People Ops, and budget requests to accounting as necessary for grant applications and reporting.
Establish review processes and timelines with the CDO and/or ED as needed for each grant report project to ensure quality and timeliness.
Maintain a grants management calendar to track deadlines and ensure timely completion of all deliverables.

Prospect Research and Portfolio Maintenance (25%)
Conduct prospect research to identify single and multi-year institutional funding opportunities.
Cultivate pathways for introductions to potential institutional donors and create prospect profiles for frontline fundraisers.
Support the CDO and ED with maintaining relationships with institutional donors through regular communication, event invites, and impact updates.
Work closely with program staff to understand funding needs and priorities, and align fundraising efforts with programmatic goals.
Manage the financial aspects of institutional giving, including budgeting and forecasting for the portfolio.

Communications (25%)
Partner with the full organizational team to write content for BTNY’s monthly newsletter, social media, and other external-facing materials.
Establish a community spotlight roster in collaboration with CDO, interview BTNY community members, write profiles and blog posts.
Assist development team with written content for solicitation letters and proposals.

THE PERSON

While these are not all requirements, the right candidate is likely to see themselves in the examples below. These examples are designed to help you determine if this opportunity aligns with your own strengths and sense of purpose.
You have exceptional writing and editing abilities, are capable of crafting compelling narratives that effectively communicate the organization's mission, goals, and impact to potential funders. You can adapt your writing style to meet varied funder needs.
You have the ability to break down and sequence large projects into manageable pieces for yourself and others - seeing the big picture, but executing on the details (i.e. developing and implementing project plans; creating and testing data collection instruments, writing and reviewing reports). 
You thrive in environments with tight deadlines, and manage your time efficiently to ensure that grant deliverables are submitted on time and accurately.

You are a team player and value both external feedback and self-reflection.

Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

OVERVIEW OF THE COMPANY

FOX Entertainment With a legacy spanning nearly 40 years, FOX Entertainment is one of the world’s most recognizable media brands and a leading global creator of multi-genre content across broadcast, streaming, digital and emerging platforms. Known for its independent, innovative spirit and bold storytelling, the company is committed to reaching audiences where they are through a platform- and format-agnostic approach to developing, testing and scaling intellectual property worldwide. FOX Entertainment consists of three core business units. The FOX Television Network, which encompasses its flagship linear platform and streaming partnerships with Hulu and FOX One, is home to hit series including The Simpsons, The Masked Singer, Doc, Memory of a Killer, Fear Factor: House of Fear, The Floor and Hell’s Kitchen. FOX Entertainment Studios, operates the in-house scripted and unscripted studios behind series such as Animal Control, Best Medicine, The Faithful, and The Way Home, as well as Bento Box Entertainment with animated hits such as Hazbin Hotel and Krapopolis; Studio Ramsay Global with Next Level Chef, Gordon Ramsay’s Secret Service and Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars; entertainment studio TMZ; and the independent film label Tideline. FOX Entertainment Global is the company’s worldwide content sales and distribution arm. As part of its evolution into a modern next-gen studio, FOX Entertainment is expanding its digital storytelling ecosystem with investments across vertical video with Holywater, Chain’s experiential storytelling, podcasting with Meet Cute, a two-way content pipeline with HarperCollins Publishing, and creator-led formats through the newly formed FOX Creator Studios. Through these strategic initiatives, the company is investing earlier in emerging ideas and new forms of audience engagement, while maintaining the ability to grow successful concepts into premium franchises across broadcast, streaming and global platforms. A prolific content creator and production partner, FOX Entertainment collaborates with leading studios, creators, and platforms worldwide to produce and distribute premium content at scale across broadcast, streaming, and digital ecosystems, while continuing to grow its portfolio of owned IP and next-generation storytelling formats.

JOB DESCRIPTION

Fox Entertainment is seeking an Executive Director, Business & Legal Affairs to lead and support a broad range of strategic dealmaking and legal matters across creator partnerships, production, and emerging technology initiatives. This role will serve as a senior legal and business advisor, partnering closely with business and legal affairs leadership and key stakeholders to structure, negotiate, and execute complex agreements in a rapidly evolving media landscape.

The department sits at the intersection of traditional entertainment, the creator economy, and technology-driven production. The ideal candidate is a highly versatile, business-minded executive who thrives in an entrepreneurial environment within a large media company. This individual combines strong strategic judgment with the ability to independently manage a high volume of complex, day-to-day matters; build trusted relationships with internal and external stakeholders; and develop practical solutions that advance business objectives while appropriately managing risk.

Regular, on-site attendance at the workplace for a minimum of four (4) days per week is an essential function of the position. The selected candidate must be able to reliably meet this requirement.

A SNAPSHOT OF YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

Support the negotiation, drafting, and execution of a broad range of complex agreements, including creator, production, talent, licensing, content, and technology-related deals
Serve as a legal and business advisor to internal stakeholders, providing practical counsel on deal structure, business strategy, contractual terms, and legal and commercial risk
Partner cross-functionally with production, ad sales, technology, finance, business development, and other teams to structure and execute partnerships and strategic initiatives
